A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, regret bounds, and mathematical proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout. Its new appendix extensions contain mathematical arguments rather than empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–5 retain their procedures. Appendix C.7 adds a sub-Gaussian adaptation that conditions parameter updates on observed rewards lying within a specified range, introducing a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts training or evaluation experiments. The sub-Gaussian extension changes theoretical scope, not evaluated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The retained comparisons with Agarwal et al. and Atsidakou et al., and the added cascading-bandit discussion, concern theoretical positioning.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols or settings. Appendix C.6 introduces a mathematical regret definition for a probability guarantee, not an empirical evaluation metric.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity studies, or empirical case analyses. Appendix C.7 is an analytical extension rather than a robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, error bars, or statistical tests. The new high-probability regret argument belongs to theory rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries, scores, rankings, or observed trends appear in either version. The added mathematical guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Remark 3.1.4 and new Appendix C.6 extend the non-contextual analysis to a high-probability O-tilde(sqrt(nT)) guarantee using Freedman's inequality and regret without the outer expectation. Appendix C.7 adds a sub-Gaussian tail-reduction argument. These are limited extensions; the central theorems, regret rates, and existing proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution summary retain the same central claims: near-optimal O-tilde(sqrt(nT)) regret for non-contextual Pandora's Box, O-tilde(nd sqrt(T)) contextual regret, and corresponding Prophet Inequality extensions.

C2.justification: Section 5 now explicitly identifies the sqrt(n) Prophet optimality gap, discusses an n-independent O-tilde(T^(2/3)) explore-then-commit alternative, and separates open questions about contextual n and d dependence. The new boundedness footnote and Appendix C.7 also broaden the stated applicability to sub-Gaussian rewards.

D1.justification: Appendix C.7 supplies the explicit reward cutoff magnitude K_i sqrt(2 log(2T^2 n)) and the associated condition for updating parameters. These provide concrete processing instructions for the new adaptation; the existing algorithm specifications are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds Kveton et al. (2015) and distinguishes user-controlled stopping in cascading bandits from policy-controlled inspection. v2 also clarifies earlier benchmark and feedback assumptions and develops implications of Jin et al. (2024), which was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds local terminology and feedback clarifications, makes Section 3's non-contextual scope explicit, reorganizes future work into two numbered questions, and adds acknowledgments and two appendix subsections. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm boxes are repositioned, including Algorithm 2 moving from page 5 to page 6, and several equations are reformatted, including the main regret definition becoming inline. The appendix contents expands, but no figures or results tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by explaining the unresolved Prophet regret gap and distinguishing the work from cascading bandits. The new theoretical extensions add useful scope, although C.7 remains a brief sketch and C.6 contains a variance expression inconsistent with its preceding definition. The gains are limited, with the central algorithms and results retained.
